content.text: No exclusivity obligation binding Corio appears anywhere in the agreement — the licences are expressly nonexclusive, the marketing exhibit is non-binding, and Corio retains freedom to resell/subcontract.

input.quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, "sole supplier" or requirements obligation on Corio (our party), meeting the preferred position. Every licence to Corio is expressly nonexclusive (Sections 2.1-2.4, 12.3), Section 2.7 restricts only use/reverse-engineering of the Software rather than sourcing from other vendors, and Section 14.8 confirms Corio "shall solely direct the provision of Corio Services and may subcontract certain portions ... to third parties." The Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation commitments are stated to be "non-binding" and so create no de facto exclusive-promotion obligation; the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and Customer definitions limit the scope of the licence granted to Corio rather than restricting Corio's freedom to buy elsewhere. The only exclusivity-flavoured provisions run in our favour (Section 2.4: Commerce One may not contact Corio Customers regarding non-ASP licence sales and must refer them to Corio), which we do not flag.
